Norwegian Floods Disrupt Business Operations Nationwide; Aker BP ASA Among Firms Hit

Severe flooding across southern Norway has disrupted economic activity nationwide, with companies from energy to shipping reporting impacts as torrential rains continue. The deluge, attributed to record rainfall over the past week, has triggered landslides, submerged key transport links, and forced the closure of major infrastructure, including sections of the E6 highway and critical rail lines.

Among those affected is Aker BP ASA, which confirmed on Thursday that operations at several of its onshore support facilities have been temporarily suspended due to flooding and logistical constraints. “Employee safety is our top priority,” a spokesperson said. “We are monitoring the situation closely and are in close dialogue with local authorities.” The company did not provide an estimate for when normal operations might resume.

The Norwegian National Business Federation reported that at least 400 businesses in the region are experiencing significant disruption, with supply chain delays and property damage compounding the challenges. “We have not seen flooding of this magnitude in decades,” said federation director Lena Haug. “Many firms are struggling to move goods, and there is a real risk of prolonged economic effects if the weather does not improve soon.”

Hydroelectric power output has also been affected, with the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate warning of potential supply interruptions if water levels continue to rise. The Port of Nordvik, a key hub for exports, has temporarily halted operations after access roads were rendered impassable.

Analysts at Nordic Market Insights estimate that the flooding could shave as much as 0.2% off Norway’s GDP growth this quarter, depending on the duration of the disruption. “The situation is highly fluid,” said chief analyst Erik Mathisen. “While Norway is well-prepared for adverse weather, the scale of these floods is testing the resilience of businesses and infrastructure alike.”

Authorities have urged residents and businesses to remain vigilant, as meteorologists forecast continued heavy rainfall in the coming days.
